title: Moonpath rollcall and telemetry sprintlet notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working runbook for the 'Moonpath' micro-release (model routing + KV cache tuning). Primary goal: safely push routing heuristics and a small KV cache optimization to hosted and dedicated fleets with minimal latency regression. Use this doc as the day-of checklist, calendar, and release-notes draft.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Scope: routing policy change (route-by-region fallback), minor KV-cache config change (ttl bump + shard tweak). No model weights.
- Target windows: low-traffic window in NA morning (UTC 14:00-17:00) and a follow-up warmup in APAC low-traffic (UTC 00:00-03:00).
- Risk level: moderate (latency sensitivity). Canary + staged traffic ramp required.
- Rollback: instant route-policy revert + flush KV prefix in 2 minutes (script included).

Calendar (high level):
- 2026-05-11 09:00 UTC: Preflight sync (ops + SRE + serving-runtime). Quick checklist run.
- 2026-05-12 14:00 UTC: Canary start (NA, 0.5% traffic -> 5% over 20 minutes).
- 2026-05-12 15:00 UTC: Canary review checkpoint (15 minutes of steady telemetry).
- 2026-05-12 16:00 UTC: Ramp to 20% if green (rolling increases every 10m).
- 2026-05-14 00:00 UTC: APAC warm window (repeat canary).
- 2026-05-15 00:00 UTC: Full rollout decision meeting (go/no-go).

Preflight checklist (day -3 to day 0):
- [ ] RE-4123 and RE-4188 merged and CI green (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Deployment manifests built and stored in release bucket (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Smoke test harness updated for new routing flags (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Canary cohort configured in routing-layer (owner: serving-runtime).
- [ ] Rollback playbook verified in staging - run rollback dry run (owner: eng-sre).
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (customer-success, support, infra) with expected windows and SLAs.
- [ ] Post-release eval prompt set created in Optimize with representative prompt set.

Day-of runbook (short actionable):
1) Start: 14:00 UTC - Moonpath canary kickoff
   - Post status to #release-ops with short payload (canary ID, cohorts, contact list).
   - Enable canary routing flag at 0.5% traffic for NA.
2) Observe: first 10 minutes
   - Watch 95th/99th p99 latency for text gen endpoints (key routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat).
   - Error rate threshold: >0.1% 5m error spike -> pause and investigate.
   - Token cost delta: expect <2% variation. If >5% abort.
3) Checkpoint 15m
   - Manual check by release lead (Ravi) + SRE (Liam).
   - If stable, increment to 5% and continue staged ramp.
4) Ramp pattern: 0.5 -> 5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100 (only if telemetry stays within thresholds).

Critical telemetry to watch (dashboards):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 overall and per-region (NA/EU/APAC).
- Errors: 4xx/5xx breakdowns, rate per route.
- Throughput: requests/s and token/s (sudden drops can indicate routing misconfig).
- Backend saturation: GPU queue length, CPU steal, kernel failures.
- Business signals: API quota errors surfaced to customers, spike in Support tickets (monitor #support-escalations).

Alarm thresholds (quick):
- Latency p95 increase >15% baseline for 10m -> pause ramp, investigate.
- Error rate >0.1% absolute increase for 5m -> rollback candidate.
- GPU queue length >5s per request average -> immediate rollback.

Rollback procedure (fast):
- Step 1: Revert routing flag to previous (tag: moonpath-v0) via rollout API (owner: Ravi).
- Step 2: Trigger KV prefix flush script (scripts/kv_flush_moonpath.sh) in affected clusters (owner: LEO oncall).
- Step 3: Notify #release-ops and #sre and open an incident in PagerDuty.
- Step 4: Collect traces and heap snapshots from 2 affected hosts; attach to JIRA RE-4188 for triage.

Post-rollout actions (immediate):
- Keep elevated telemetry sampling for 48h (trace rate x2 for changed routes).
- Run Optimize evals overnight; compare perplexity and output quality across representative prompts.
- Draft final release notes in the channel and link to Confluence.
- Schedule a 1-hour retro within 72h (owner: Ravi).

Draft release notes (internal -> public):
Title: Moonpath routing improvement and KV-cache tuning
What changed:
- Routing: added region-aware fallback prioritization to reduce cross-region model hops. Expected to reduce cold-starts for large-context sessions.
- KV-cache: increased prefix TTL for short-lived keys and reduced shard contention under high QPS.
Impact:
- Expected: improved tail latency for multi-turn chat in NA/EU; slight performance improvement for repeated prompts.
- Customer visible changes: none to prompt/response format; no model output semantics intentionally changed.
Rollback instructions (public):
- We maintain an immediate rollback path; if you observe increased latency please contact support with request ID.
Known issues and caveats:
- Short-lived edge-case where prefix TTL bump may increase memory footprint during warmup periods (monitoring enabled).
- Rare routing misassignment on older SDK versions - SDKs older than 1.3.2 may not receive fallback hints properly.

Open questions / TODOs (pin here):
- Can we add a soft-fallback telemetry tag to correlate SDK version -> routing success? (owner: Maya)
- Validate memory footprint on smallest Dedicated pools (1xA100) under synthetic spike (owner: infra).
- Confirm billing impact baseline with Finance (token delta) and sign-off on cost gating.

Notes from preflight sync (2026-05-03):
- Serving-runtime reported kernel selection stable for this change; kernel fallback not touched.
- Observability: need to add a derived metric 'routing-fallback-rate' to each model route (action: SRE data-instrumentation ticket).
- Support asked for a short blurb for customer comms that we can publicize if rollout completes without incident.

Small scripts / snippets to keep handy (in repo):
- scripts/rollout_toggle.sh --canary-id moonpath --set 0.5
- scripts/kv_flush_moonpath.sh --region na-east-1 --prefix moonpath-v2
- scripts/check_telemetry_snapshot.sh --since 10m --metric p95_latency

Communication plan (who to ping):
- Exec on-call: Maya Chen (pager), Ravi Patel (release lead), Liam O'Connor (sre lead), Sofia Martinez (runtime lead).
- Channels: #release-ops (public updates), #sre (technical), #support-escalations (customer-facing issues).
- Customers: targeted emails only if we hit rollback or >1% customer-facing errors.

Retro prompts (post-release):
- What signal delayed ramping and why?
- Was the rollback path exercised and how long did it take?
- Any telemetry gaps we discovered?
- Action items for automating rollback on routing flag failure.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- RE-4123: routing policy implementation (design notes).
- RE-4188: KV cache change (benchmarks attached).
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 (merge commit abcdef).

(End of working draft - keep editing in place. This doc is intentionally informal; move to a polished release note in Confluence once final.)
